notes: Revision of a stored fact on a functional relation (sequel_of, which is a subproperty of follows_in_series). Related near: functional (it is no longer the sequel to The Hobbit); related far: a composition on a fact that does not come from The Lord of the Rings itself (the year the book it continues was published: 1937 becomes 1871), replacing a who-wrote-it question that 'sequels share their prequel's author' leaves at Tolkien; derived: transitivity through precedes_in_series (Alice's Adventures in Wonderland precedes Through the Looking-Glass, which now precedes The Lord of the Rings; asked as whether Alice comes earlier in the same book series; an earlier 'reading the books in order' wording was dropped because publication order already puts Alice first) and two compositions about Through the Looking-Glass. The indeterminate question splits on whether the advice to read The Hobbit first is stored under its title or as 'read the book the sequel continues' (the earlier question about the One Ring was dropped: it put the Ring into Carroll's book, which contradicts what models hold of it). Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma except those marked approximate. Pairing: contraction removes "The Lord of the Rings is the sequel to The Hobbit." (functional); expansion keeps sequel_of and Through the Looking-Glass with a made-up book. After review: the related far year accepts 1871 or 1872 (Wikipedia says December 1871, the title page 1872); the reading-advice rule is rated a stored, defeasible convention (counts above), not a definition, so a world that keeps 'read The Hobbit first' is consistent.
